items.label: Bakery breakfast
items.note: Berlin lets bakeries sell baked goods from 07:00 to 16:00 on holidays. The queue peaks mid-morning, so go before 09:30 or after 14:00.

items.label: Full grocery run
items.note: Regular supermarkets stay closed. Station shops carry the day: REWE Ostbahnhof 06:00 to 24:00, REWE Hauptbahnhof and EDEKA Friedrichstrasse roughly 08:00 to 22:00.

items.label: KaDeWe, malls, big stores
items.note: Closed on 3 October, and Sunday 4 October is closed anyway. Move real shopping to Friday 2 October.

items.label: Museum visit
items.note: The state museums open as on a Sunday, most from 10:00 to 18:00. Museum shops open with them, which quietly solves souvenirs.

items.label: Cafe or brunch table
items.note: Cafes run a normal weekend service, and a holiday Saturday is their busiest shift. Go before 10:00 or reserve.

items.label: Pharmacy errand
items.note: Regular pharmacies close, but one per area is on emergency duty around the clock. Look up the current Notdienst pharmacy on aponet.de.

items.label: Restaurant dinner
items.note: Restaurants treat 3 October like any strong Saturday. Book a table; the holiday weekend fills the good rooms first.

items.label: Club night
items.note: A completely normal Berlin club Saturday, and TAG DER CLUBKULTUR opens that same night across dozens of venues.

items.label: Airport transfer (BER)
items.note: Trains run the Sunday timetable all day, S9 and FEX included. The REWE in Terminal 1 opens 05:00 to 24:00 if you land hungry.

items.label: Cash from a bank
items.note: Bank branches stay shut. ATMs run around the clock; stick to bank-branded machines and skip the blue convenience ATMs.
